answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a public registry before it may submit jobs, with rewards and reputation tied to that same vertex over time. A newcomer cannot instantly inherit a trusted history, and suspicious clusters can be rate-limited until their links are reviewed. The lock is released only after a delay, so creating and cycling thousands of fake identities ties up capital and exposes it to slashing for provable fraud. A violet pigment label might mark unverified accounts, but the defense is the costly, persistent bond—not the label.
